transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Authorities in the UK say they have foiled a suspected terror plot.
A group of men were arrested near an air base the U.S. has used for attacks on Iran.
NPR's Lauren Freire explains what happened.
A farmer who lives nearby called police in the middle of the night to say she noticed
three suspicious vans with masked men.
Police intercepted the vehicles, arrested five men on suspicion, they say,
of explosives and terrorism offenses.
Police say an Iran link is just one of the possibilities they're investigating.
The government here has also accused Russia of plotting attacks on British soil.
But this past summer, Iran did threaten British bases.
NPR's Lauren Freire reporting.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi this weekend
to meet with the leader of the United Arab Emirates.
That's according to a person briefed on the matter.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports from Tel Aviv.
The person was not authorized to speak publicly
and did not say what came out of Netanyahu's meeting with UAE leader Mohammed bin Zayed.
The United Arab Emirates has not commented on the matter.
This comes after first Haaretz newspaper in Israel and then the New York Times reported
that shortly before the October 7th attacks in 2023,
the Emirati leader had warned Netanyahu that Hamas was planning an attack.
NPR has not independently confirmed the reporting and Netanyahu's office denies it.
The October 7th attacks and the question of accountability for the Israeli security failure
are a leading topic as Netanyahu seeks reelection next month.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
President Trump is refusing to send hundreds of millions of dollars
to the places Congress says it has to go.
The move is called a pocket rescission.
The federal government's nonpartisan watchdog,
the Government Accountability Office, says the president's maneuver is illegal
and beers Eric McDaniel reports.
Each year, Congress passes laws which allocate money to the federal government's various programs and agencies.
That is their constitutional responsibility, the power of the purse.
Now, the executive branch is unilaterally withholding money owed to programs the president opposes.
That's $560 million to programs that provide services to refugees and other immigrants,
according to a memo from the White House.
Also, $15 million to a Justice Department team tasked with preventing and resolving racial tensions.
That's $70 million to programs providing grants and fellowships to support institutions,
bringing foreign students and faculty to the U.S.,
and tens of millions more to initiatives that touch on climate change or racial and gender minority work.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News in Washington.
The White House started airing a new ad this weekend featuring President Trump.
In it, he asks people to join him in his fight to expel warmongers from the government.
The ad says it was paid for by the U.S. government.
Critics say this appears to violate federal law.
This is NPR.
China and the U.S. have agreed to reduce tariffs on certain goods worth $30 billion in each direction.
This comes after President Xi's state visit to the U.S. last week.
China will lower its tariffs on some U.S. products such as beef, almonds, coal, and medical equipment.
The U.S. will lower tariffs on certain Chinese products such as baby items, toys, and decorations.
The zoo in Atlanta has welcomed two new giant pandas.
The loan from China is part of a new agreement between the U.S. and Chinese governments.
NPR's Kristin Wright reports.
Male panda ping-ping, who's six, and female fu-shuang, who's five, flew in on Boeing's FedEx Panda Express jet.
The giant pandas will stay in quarantine for about a month in Zoo Atlanta's new panda complex
before they're introduced to the public on a date to be announced later.
Ping-ping and fu-shuang are in Atlanta for 10 years,
through a new conservation agreement between the zoo and the China Wildlife Conservation Association.
China's President Xi Jinping officially confirmed the pandas would soon arrive during his visit to Washington last week.
Zoo Atlanta is one of three zoos in the U.S. with pandas on loan from China.
Once endangered, they're now classified as vulnerable species.
Kristin Wright, NPR News.
The National Weather Service says a powerful nor'easter will weaken tonight.
Heavy rain and near-hurricane forest winds hit the east coast this weekend from the mid-Atlantic up in New England.
It is still raining heavily in the northeast.
Separately, Hawaii is recovering after Hurricane Nolo brushed the Big Island.
It never made landfall, but poured very heavy rain.
I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News.

topics.text: UK authorities arrest five men near US air base on suspicion of explosives and terrorism offenses
Israeli PM Netanyahu secretly traveled to Abu Dhabi to meet UAE leader Mohammed bin Zayed
President Trump refuses to send hundreds of millions of dollars Congress allocated to various federal programs
White House airs new ad featuring President Trump asking people to expel warmongers from government
China and US agree to reduce tariffs on certain goods worth $30 billion in each direction
Atlanta Zoo receives two giant pandas on loan from China under new conservation agreement
Powerful nor'easter weakens after bringing heavy rain and near-hurricane winds to US east coast
Hurricane Nolo brushes Hawaii's Big Island, causing heavy rain but no reported landfall
